reports.lens: DATA INTEGRITY: raw-bar sanity, splits and distributions, alignment, NVDL vs NVDX divergence, cross-check against fresh Robinhood data and the NVDA/META underlyings, and a recomputation of the BASKET-20261013 numbers
key_findings: The raw NVDL data is clean, so the NVDA-2x overnight edge is not a data artifact. All 15 symbols have exactly the 258 expected NYSE sessions (2025-10-01..2026-10-09): 0 duplicates, 0 missing days, 0 interpolated bars, 0 bars where high/low are inconsistent with open/close, and 0 zero-volume bars. walkfwd.py's date intersection drops 0 dates. The on-disk NVDL/NVDX/METU bars match a fresh split-adjusted Robinhood pull exactly (0 mismatches across 258 bars each).

The edge sits in the underlying itself. NVDA close-to-open averaged +0.245% per night (sd 1.40, win 58.8%, cumulative +83%), while NVDA open-to-close went -33% cumulative over the same 257 nights. NVDL overnight equals 2x NVDA overnight with a residual of -0.032% per night (sd 0.168, beta 1.98, correlation 0.998). The NVDA-2x overnight edge is genuine in the data.

NVDL did a 3:1 forward split effective 2026-06-26 (raw 'none' prices are exactly 3.0x the split-adjusted prices before that date). The split-adjusted series handles it correctly: the 6/26 night is -2.77%, consistent with NVDA's move. No fake -50%/+100% nights appear in any of the 15 names.

The doc's headline numbers reproduce exactly. NVDL last 250 nights: +0.441%, sd 2.81, median +0.461%, win 57.2%, cumulative +173%. NVDX last 250: +0.401%, cumulative +146%. METU last 250: +0.041%, sd 3.67, median -0.058%, win 48.4%, cumulative -7%. Walk-forward fixed NVDL on 137 nights: +0.459%, sd 2.71. NVDL is positive in 9 of 13 months. NVDL ex-earnings is +0.390%.

NVDX has two data defects, and both make NVDX look worse than it is. (1) 2025-12-24 is a distribution ex-date of about 3.1% (the 'all' adjustment factor steps from 0.9686 to 1.0 that day). The split-only data books it as an overnight loss: NVDX -4.32% against 2x NVDA -1.34%. (2) The 2026-09-08 daily open of 20.85 is a bad print. The first 1-minute bar opened at 21.79, so the night shows -1.88% when the true figure is about +2.5%. Corrected, NVDX is +0.448% over 257 nights and +0.431% over the last 250, essentially equal to NVDL.

METU pays quarterly distributions of about 0.5-0.7% (ex-dates around 12/23, 3/24, 6/23 and 9/22). They show up as fake overnight drops of -0.84, -0.68, -0.89 and -0.61% against 2x META. This understates METU by only about 0.012% per night and changes no conclusion.

Error in the doc: METU ex-earnings is +0.190% per night (+0.193% over the last 250), not the stated +0.02%. Its median is -0.044% and the 5/5-trimmed mean is +0.07%. It is positive in 8 of 13 months ex-earnings (6 of 13 including all nights), not 5 of 13. The doc's figure can only be reproduced by excluding the wrong night (the night before each pm report, which gives +0.043%) instead of the night ending at the next morning's open.

Biggest problem: the basket comparison counts earnings nights that both rulebooks black out. METU's four earnings nights total about -37% (-22.1, +21.0, -15.4, -20.7) and NVDL's total about +19% (+9.7, +12.3, -1.7, -1.2). With cash on each name's own earnings nights, as §3 and v1.5(d) require: over 257 nights the old basket (2/3 METU + 1/3 NVDL) makes +0.253% per night (sd 2.17, score 0.116) against NVDL alone at +0.384% (sd 2.62, score 0.147), a difference of +0.131% per night with t = 1.01. In the 137-night test window the old basket is better: +0.432% (score 0.187) against +0.379% (score 0.151). Over the last 60 nights they are tied (0.305 vs 0.306). The doc's line that the current basket is 'the worst in every window' does not hold once the blackout is applied.

Choosing NVDA as the core is hindsight. An expanding-window rule picking the best long-history overnight score each week (the same criterion v1.5 uses) never picks NVDL in a walk-forward: it holds MUU for 137 nights and TSMX for 60. At full sample, MUU has a higher t-stat (2.67) than NVDL (2.64). A joint bootstrap across the 14 names puts the probability of a max-t at least as large as NVDL's at 0.032.

Rule (b) is misapplied and knife-edge. On the agent's own research data (through 10/9), MUU qualifies: 250-night score 0.1598 against the core's 0.1572, and ex-earnings mean +0.96%, well above +0.25%. It still qualifies with 10/12 included (0.1510 vs 0.1496). It fails only once the -11.1% MUU night of 10/13 is added (0.1474 vs 0.1530). 'None qualifies on 10/13' was not true when the research was written, and the rule will flip from week to week.

The NVDL edge is concentrated. Dropping the 10 best nights cuts the mean to +0.196%; dropping the best 20 cuts it to +0.018%. Bootstrap 95% CI for the mean is [+0.12%, +0.79%] (block-10 bootstrap: [+0.13%, +0.74%]). The first half of the sample is +0.385% (t 1.54), the second half +0.531% (t 2.21).

Entry and exit timing do not create the edge. On 5-minute bars (161 nights, 2026-02-23..10-13), NVDL close-to-open (the model) is +0.325%, 15:50-to-09:30 is +0.266%, and 15:50-to-09:35 is +0.321%. The 15:50-to-official-close drift is -0.04%. So the timing bias is at most about 0.06% per night.

The live out-of-sample record does not favour the switch, though the samples are tiny. 19 live NVDL overnight legs averaged -0.053% against +0.105% for the model on the same nights. 21 METU legs averaged +0.588% live against +0.663% model.

recommended_changes: Redo the BASKET-20261013 §3 basket table and the 'expected effect' with the earnings blackout applied to both baskets (cash or substitute on each name's own earnings night), since that is how both rulebooks trade. With the blackout, the honest uplift is about +0.13% per night over 257 nights (about $0.14 a night at E=$105), not +0.22%, and it is about -0.05% in the 137-night test window.
Correct METU ex-earnings to +0.19% per night, 8 of 13 months positive. Always exclude the night that ends at the open after a pm report.

Resolve rule (b): MUU met it with data through 10/9 and 10/12. Either state that MUU qualified and was rejected for a stated reason (sd 6-7% a night), or add a volatility cap and hysteresis (for example, beat the core score by at least 0.02 for 2 consecutive Monday re-ranks) so the satellite decision does not flip week to week on one night.

Clean NVDX before using m_NVDX in v1.5(c) sizing: add back the 2025-12-24 distribution (about 3.1%) and replace the 2026-09-08 daily open with 21.79 (first 1-minute bar). Corrected NVDX is +0.43-0.45%, about equal to NVDL. More generally, use dividend-aware overnight returns or flag ex-dates. Expect another NVDX December distribution: holding across the ex-date is not a loss because the cash is received, but the model and the P&L tracker must not count the price drop as one.

Present the edge as about +0.35-0.45% per night with a 95% CI of roughly [+0.12%, +0.79%], heavily dependent on the top 10-20 nights. Say plainly that NVDA was chosen with hindsight, because no ex-ante long-window rule would have picked it.

Add an edge-decay and kill check specific to v1.5: live NVDL legs so far average -0.05% (n=19). Review after about 20 NVDA-2x nights, comparing the realised mean against the blackout-adjusted old-basket counterfactual.
Define what happens on half-day sessions (2026-11-27 and 2026-12-24 close at 13:00), since a 15:52 entry is impossible on those days.
caveats: Robinhood's adjustment_type 'all' for daily bars shows daily factor jitter (for example, NVDA's factor moves 0.997-0.999 although its dividend is tiny), consistent with the tool's note that 'all' is intraday-only. I used it only to locate large distribution steps, not for returns.

Intraday 30-minute bars are interpolated (filler) before about 2026-01-30, and the 5-minute data starts 2026-02-23. The timing-bias check therefore covers 161 nights, not the full year, and uses 15:50/15:55 and 09:30/09:35 as proxies for the live 15:52 and 09:31:05 times.
The 9/8 NVDX correction uses the 09:30 one-minute bar's open (21.79) as the true open. The official opening print was not available.
In the blackout comparison, blacked-out legs sit in cash. The old rule would have substituted the next-ranked name, which could move the old basket either way.
Live-trade samples are tiny (19 NVDL legs, 21 METU legs, 5 NVDX legs), and their pnl/pct columns in trades.csv are inconsistently ordered, so I recomputed returns from the entry and exit prices.
I did not test whether NVDA's overnight drift will persist. The data integrity lens can only confirm that the drift is really in the historical data.

reports.lens: LOOK-AHEAD / SELECTION BIAS: strict walk-forward and split-sample test of whether an ex-ante version of v1.5 would have picked NVDA-2x and profited
key_findings: Choosing NVDA is hindsight. No ex-ante version of v1.5's own logic picks NVDA. Method: at each monthly rebalance, pick the top underlying by long-window overnight score, with or without the ex-earnings mean > +0.25% filter, using only prior nights. Over 0 of 10 months (expanding window, Jan to Oct 2026) and 0 of 7 months (120-night window, Apr to Oct) it chose NVDA. Expanding window picked MUU for 26-01, 26-02 and 26-06 to 26-10, and TSMX for 26-03 to 26-05. The 120-night window picked MUU, TSMX, MUU, MUU, MUU, TNA, TNA. The ex-earnings filter changes nothing, because MUU and TSMX clear 0.25% easily.

The rule as a procedure, not the NVDA choice, does about half as well out of sample. Percent-of-E basis: from 2026-01-02 (193 nights), score 0.064 (mean +0.381%, sd 5.95, cum +47.5%). Fixed NVDL with earnings blackout: score 0.142 (mean +0.350%, sd 2.47, cum +85.1%). EW14: score 0.107. Whole-share, affordability-aware sim at E=$100: generic rule score 0.074 at 77% invested; hindsight NVDA-2x 0.140 (+0.329% of E per night, 94% invested).

NVDA only comes out if you add a volatility cap that was tuned with hindsight. The cap would have to sit near NVDL's own sd of about 2.8%. Cap 3%: NVDA picked 8/10 months (OOS score 0.102 from January). Cap 3.5%: 6/10 (0.136). Cap 4%: 1/10 (0.101). No cap: 0/10 (0.064). The agent's stated reason for dropping MUU (sd 6-7% and fat earnings tails) is exactly that unpublished hindsight filter.

Split sample. Choosing on Oct 2025 to Mar 2026 (125 nights): TSMX ranks #1 (0.187), MUU #2 (0.179), NVDL #3 (0.158). The ex-ante pick, TSMX, then scores 0.126 on Apr to Oct (132 nights). On those nights fixed NVDL scores 0.152 and EW14 0.160, so the ex-ante choice loses to a no-selection equal-weight basket. Reverse direction: choosing on H2 picks NVDL, which scores 0.142 on H1 vs EW 0.115. NVDL ranks in the top 3 in both halves, but so does MUU (#2 in both).

NVDL's edge over the universe is not statistically distinguishable. Paired NVDL minus EW14: +0.112%/night, t=1.09 (full sample); H1 +0.179 (t=1.25); H2 +0.048 (t=0.33); excluding NVDA earnings nights +0.068 (t=0.71). Studentized reality check (13 underlyings, stationary bootstrap) vs EW: NVDL adjusted p=0.83. Against zero, NVDL survives data-snooping only marginally (adjusted p=0.042). The overnight drift looks universe-wide: EW14 full-sample score is 0.139 vs NVDL 0.165.

The top score is about what best-of-13 luck produces. Null: every underlying has the same true score, with cross-correlation kept. Under it, E[max score] = 0.187, and P(max >= 0.165) = 0.66. Observed max-minus-mean gap is 0.076 vs a null expectation of 0.081 (p=0.47). Cross-sectional score dispersion is not significantly above correlated noise (p=0.18). Empirical-Bayes shrinkage factor is 0.33, which shrinks NVDL's score from 0.165 to 0.115 (universe mean 0.091).

Long-window rank has no predictive power out of sample. Mean monthly Spearman IC (window score vs next-month score, 13 underlyings): W30 +0.018, W60 +0.003, W120 +0.010, expanding +0.088 (t=0.71). The long window that v1.5 relies on predicts no better than the 30-night rank it replaced.
There is no out-of-sample evidence for the 250-night criterion. With 257 nights on disk, a 250-night window exists for only the last 6 OOS nights. Every number behind the core choice is in-sample.

v1.5's satellite gate is a knife-edge, and on the agent's own data file it fires. On the 250 nights ending at the 10/9 open, MUU scores 0.160 vs NVDL 0.157, and MUU's ex-earnings mean is +0.96%, so MUU qualifies under §3(b). Adding the 10/12 open (Monday re-rank) gives MUU 0.151 vs NVDL 0.150, still qualifying. Only after MUU's -11.1% night into the 10/13 open does it fall to 0.147 vs 0.153. The research doc's 'none qualifies on 10/13' depends on one night.
The ex-earnings > +0.25% bar is applied only to satellites, never to the core. NVDL itself fails it at 3/7 monthly rebalances on a 120-night window and 4/10 on a 60-night window.

The persistence evidence is not specific to NVDA. 'NVDL positive in 9 of 13 months' also holds for 9 of 14 names and for EW14; SOXL and TQQQ are positive in 10. NVDL's quarterly rank was 7, 2, 11, 1, and its monthly rank ranged from 1 to 13. The decision came right after NVDL's best quarter (Jul to Oct, rank 1, score 0.261 vs EW 0.117), the same recency pattern the doc held against METU.

The agent's walkfwd.py is reproduced exactly (W30 +0.391%, score 0.078; NVDL 0.169; EW 0.165). But 'the 30-night rank is the weakest rule' depends on the weekly phase: across the 5 weekly phases, W30 scores range 0.078 to 0.138 (mean +0.40% to +0.74%/night). Old §3 in a realistic whole-share, affordable-only implementation is still weak: score 0.085 from January and 0.075 from April, about 68-73% invested. Leaving the old rule is supported; why NVDA in particular replaces it is not.

What still holds for v1.5: NVDA-2x was positive out of sample in both halves; fixed NVDA-2x whole-share beat the realistic old rule (0.140-0.150 vs 0.075-0.085); and NVDL's mean > 0 survives the snooping adjustment (p=0.042). The error is in claiming NVDA is uniquely persistent and in the size of the expected edge, not in the direction.

recommended_changes: Cut the stated expected edge. Shrinkage puts NVDL's score at about 0.115, which at sd ~2.7% and ~95% invested is roughly +0.30%/night, or about $0.31/night at E=$105. That is consistent with the realized out-of-sample +0.33-0.36% of E. Replace the claimed +0.44-0.46% and $0.40/night, and report the figure as an estimate with an error band, not a fact.

Rewrite the §3 rationale. NVDA was chosen with a volatility filter in mind, and that filter is not written down. Either write it as an explicit ex-ante rule (e.g. the core is the top long-window score among affordable names with trailing sd < 3.5%) and accept that it would have picked TSMX or GGLL in some months, or keep NVDA as a discretionary choice and say so.

Fix the satellite gate. It compares two noisy scores; the standard error is about 1/sqrt(250) ≈ 0.063. Require a margin of about 1 SE (score >= core + 0.06) or drop the gate. Also correct the record: on the 10/9 data file MUU passed (0.160 vs 0.157), and it failed only after the 10/13 open.
Apply the ex-earnings > +0.25% test to the core as well, or remove it. NVDL failed it in 3 of 7 monthly 120-night windows.

Consider diversifying within the whole-share budget, e.g. NVDA-2x plus one affordable lower-correlation name (TNA, FNGU or TQQQ). EW14 scored about the same as NVDL out of sample (0.160 vs 0.152 from April) and carries no selection risk.

Set a forward kill and review criterion now, before more data comes in. Example: after 40 live nights, if NVDA-2x trails an equal-weight basket of the affordable names by more than about 0.2%/night, reopen the core choice.

Stop calling the 30-night rule 'the weakest tested' on the strength of phase 0. Its weekly-phase range is 0.078-0.138. The stronger, defensible reason for dropping it is the realistic whole-share result: score 0.075-0.085 at about 70% invested.
caveats: One year of data (257 nights). Every split is short, and quarterly and monthly ranks are very noisy.

Earnings nights come from Robinhood get_earnings_results: a pm report means that date's close-to-next-open night; an am report means the prior night. The index ETFs (FNGU, SOXL, TECL, TQQQ, SPXL, TNA) get no earnings exclusion.
Returns use the 16:00 close to the 09:30 open, not the live 15:52 entry and 09:31 exit. The weekend research measured live-vs-model slippage at about 0.07% per leg.

The whole-share sim fixes E at $100 (no compounding) and approximates the old rule's v1.1 sizing. It skips unaffordable names (SPXL never affordable; TECL 6%, GGLL 43%, SOXL 54% of nights) and does not model the v1.2 NVDX partial unit.
The universe is the agent's hand-picked 14 names, which carries its own survivorship and selection. TZA is excluded.
Bootstrap results come from a stationary bootstrap with mean block length 5 and 2000-4000 draws; p-values are approximate.
The 10/12 and 10/13 bars were fetched live (get_equity_historicals) for 6 symbols only. They match the file on overlapping dates (10/8 and 10/9 checked).

key_findings: The NVDA-2x overnight edge holds up statistically at n=257. NVDL averages +0.458%/night (iid t=2.63, Newey-West t=2.90 at lag 5 and 2.93 at lag 10). Its stationary-bootstrap 90% CI is [+0.19, +0.72]% with block 5 and [+0.20, +0.72]% with block 10, and P(mean>0)=0.997-0.998. NVDX averages +0.419% (t=2.40, CI [+0.15, +0.69]). The underlying NVDA averages +0.245% (t=2.80). The edge survives a 14-name White reality check, but only just: P(max t >= 2.63)=0.033 (block 5) and 0.039 (block 10), against a 95th-percentile max-t of 2.49-2.53. That check does not count the other rule variants the agent also searched.

The size of v1.5's edge is overstated. v1.5 goes to cash on NVDA earnings nights, which removes two windfalls (+9.7% and +12.3% on NVDL; the other two earnings nights were -1.7% and -1.2%). On a rules-consistent basis NVDL is +0.384%/night (t=2.35, CI [+0.12, +0.64]). The actual night-25 holding, NVDX, is +0.346%/night (t=2.10, CI [+0.08, +0.61]), not +0.46%.

The improvement over the old basket is not statistically credible. On the raw paired comparison, NVDL minus OLD (2/3 METU + 1/3 NVDL) is +0.277%/night (t=1.63, NW t=1.49-1.58), with a 90% CI of [-0.015, +0.571] and P>0 of 0.93-0.95. NVDX minus OLD is +0.238% (t=1.39, P>0 0.89-0.91). Most of that gap comes from earnings nights that both rulebooks exclude. The old §3 blacked out METU on META earnings nights, which were -22.1%, +21.0%, -15.4% and -20.8%. With earnings handled consistently, v1.5 (cash on NVDA earnings) minus OLD (META-earnings blackout) is +0.102%/night (t=0.77, 90% CI [-0.15, +0.34], P>0 about 0.75-0.77). Excluding all earnings nights it is +0.135% (t=1.01). For the actual NVDX holding it is +0.064% (t=0.48).

In dollars, the doc's '+$0.40 vs +$0.18' framing reproduces as +$0.246/night (90% CI -$0.05 to +$0.54, P>0 0.91). On the rules-consistent basis it is +$0.071/night (90% CI -$0.19 to +$0.32, P>0 0.69). Detecting the consistent difference at 80% power would take about 2,700 nights (about 7,000 for NVDX). There are 257.

The BASKET doc misstates a fact. It says METU excluding earnings is +0.02%/night. With pm reports correctly aligned (the night that starts on the report date), it is +0.190%/night (t=1.14; median -0.044%). METU's weak +0.04% headline therefore comes mostly from four earnings nights, and the ex-earnings gap to NVDL is about 0.18%/night, not 0.37%.

The 'NVDA-specific' story is not separated from generic leveraged-ETF overnight drift. NVDL minus an equal-weight portfolio of all 14 names is +0.112%/night (t=1.09, P>0 0.82-0.84), and a reality check for any name beating that portfolio gives p=0.85. Regressed on QQQ's overnight return, NVDL's alpha is +0.226%/night (t=2.02, NW t=1.93, beta 2.58, R2 0.59); NVDX's alpha is +0.187% (t=1.65). QQQ's own overnight return is +0.09% (t=1.73). After empirical-Bayes shrinkage, NVDL's excess over the equal-weight portfolio is +0.098%.

The satellite gate in v1.5(b) sits on a knife edge and has already flipped. Over 250-night windows, MUU's score was at or above NVDL's on the window ending 10/9 (0.1598 vs 0.1572, using the doc's own data) and on the one ending 10/12 (0.1510 vs 0.1496). It fell below only on 10/13 (0.1474 vs 0.1530), after MUU's -11.1% night. MUU's mean excluding earnings is +0.87-0.96%, well above the 0.25% hurdle. The two scores differ by about 0.003-0.006, while the standard error of a 250-night score is about 0.063, so the gate is coin-flip noise and will churn.

The doc's ranking of rules is noise. The 30-night top-2 rule versus fixed NVDL over the last 137 nights differs by +0.069%/night (t=0.19, 90% CI [-0.46, +0.56], P>0 0.60). An honest walk-forward of a long-window score selector (expanding window) would have picked MUU and TSMX, not NVDL: top-1 from night 120 earned +0.959%/night (t=1.50), versus +0.459% for NVDL on the same nights. Choosing NVDL is an in-sample decision. Across the 14 names, the split-half Spearman correlation of scores is 0.21 (p=0.46), so score ranks do not persist.

The intraday claim (do not hold through the session on blocked days) is directionally plausible but not significant. NVDL open-to-close averages -0.281%/day (t=-1.17, NW t -1.18/-1.28, 90% CI [-0.66, +0.11], P(<0) about 0.88-0.90). NVDA is -0.137% (t=-1.13) and METU -0.027% (t=-0.12). Staying in cash is still justified, because holding adds about 3.9%/day of standard deviation with no evidence of a positive mean. 'NVDA-2x loses intraday' should not be stated as an established fact.

Stability is acceptable. NVDL's rolling 60-night mean was negative in 4.5% of windows (minimum -0.07%), within an iid-resample null (mean 10.2%, 90% range 0-35%). Rolling 20-night means were negative 21.8% of the time, 30-night 19.3%, and 120-night 0%. METU's rolling 60-night mean was negative 59% of the time. The halves agree in sign but neither is significant alone: H1 +0.385% (t=1.53), H2 +0.531% (t=2.20). NVDL was positive in 9 of 13 months, which has a binomial p of 0.133.

No significant regime dependence was found, but the current regime is the weaker one. With QQQ above its 50-day average (as on 10/12, +2.8%), NVDL overnight is +0.285% (t=1.40, n=165); below it, +0.745% (t=2.17, n=85), with Welch p=0.25. The NVDL-minus-OLD gap is +0.047% (t=0.22) above the average versus +0.692% (t=2.33) below it (p=0.08). Splitting on NVDA's 20-day return: up +0.568% (t=2.61), down +0.272% (t=0.94). These splits were chosen after looking at the data, so treat them as indicative.

On risk, v1.5 is not worse than the old basket. NVDL's worst night was -8.37% (5% CVaR -5.35%, max drawdown -18.3%), against -15.3% (CVaR -6.50%, max drawdown -27.7%) for the old basket including META earnings. In a 20-night stationary bootstrap, P(cumulative < 0) is 0.22 for NVDL and 0.39 for OLD; P(< -10%) is 0.052 and 0.130. But NVDL and NVDX correlate at 0.99 overnight, so the core is one asset.

Execution and tracking. Live overnight legs versus the model (close to next open) show -0.003%/leg across 45 legs (t=-0.02), so execution is not leaking. NVDL trails 2x NVDA overnight by -0.032%/night (t=-3.08). NVDL beats NVDX by +0.039%/night paired (t=1.73, bootstrap P>0 about 0.97), so NVDX x5 carries a small, persistent overnight tracking disadvantage. The sizing rule's objective already uses these means.

Replace the knife-edge satellite gate in v1.5(b) ('score >= core's'). Require statistical separation instead: for example, the paired 250-night excess over NVDL must have t >= 2, or the score must lead by at least about 0.06 (one standard error), and the name must qualify at two consecutive Monday re-ranks (hysteresis). MUU passed the literal gate on the 10/9 and 10/12 windows and failed on 10/13, which will cause churn.

Use expanding-window or empirical-Bayes shrunk means rather than raw 250-night means as m in the v1.5(c) sizing. The NVDL vs NVDX choice is driven by a 0.04%/night difference whose standard error is about 0.023%, which is acceptable. Note that NVDL's paired tracking edge over NVDX (+0.039%/night, t=1.73) slightly favours NVDL-heavy combinations when exposure is near-equal.

Pre-register a statistical review trigger instead of reacting to short runs. A 20-night NVDA-2x mean below zero happens about 23% of the time even if the edge is real, and a 60-night one about 10%. Review only if the rolling 120-night live+model mean is below zero (0% of in-sample windows) or a CUSUM test rejects the +0.35% hypothesis.
Keep cash on PDT-blocked days, but state the reason as variance with no demonstrated intraday edge (NVDL intraday t=-1.17, CI includes 0). Do not claim it is a proven loss.

Acknowledge that the edge may be generic leveraged-long overnight drift (equal-weight of 14 names +0.35%, t=2.23; NVDL excess t=1.09), with an NVDA-specific alpha of t of about 2. The core is a single asset (NVDL/NVDX correlation 0.99). Single-name concentration was chosen in-sample, and an honest long-window walk-forward would have selected MUU/TSMX instead.

Track the regime. The NVDL overnight edge and the gap over the old basket were weakest when QQQ was above its 50-day average (+0.285%, t=1.40; gap +0.05%, t=0.22), which is the current state. Watch whether live results in this regime support the edge before raising conviction or size.
caveats: The whole sample is one year (257 nights) in which NVDA's overnight cumulative was +83% and intraday -33%. One persistent anomaly drives everything, and a regime change would not show up in these block bootstraps.

Earnings alignment uses Robinhood earnings dates: NVDA, META and MU report pm, so the night starts on the report date; TSM reports am. Other agents may align differently, which changes ex-earnings figures. The METU +0.02% in the doc reproduces only roughly (+0.04%) under misalignment.

The OLD basket is modelled as fixed 2/3 METU + 1/3 NVDL, as the lens instructed. The live old rule rotated by 30-night rank (AMZU, AAPU and NVDX also appeared), and its blackout substitute would have been the next-ranked name, not necessarily NVDL.
Regime splits (QQQ 50-day average, 20-day returns) were chosen after looking at the data, and four splits were tested. p=0.08 for the gap's regime difference is not significant after multiplicity.
The reality-check p (0.033-0.039) covers only the 14-name choice, not the agent's search over windows and basket variants. With that search counted, the corrected p would be higher.
The bootstrap assumes stationarity. Block lengths of 5 and 10 gave nearly identical CIs, and Newey-West t-stats were slightly higher than iid, so autocorrelation is not driving the results.
Daily open prints differ from live 09:31 fills by up to about ±1.5% on single nights. On average over 45 live legs the difference was -0.003%, but per-leg noise is large.
The 14-name universe is itself a curated, survivorship-biased set of popular leveraged ETFs.

reports.lens: EXECUTION REALISM: live 15:52 to 09:31:05 fills vs the model's 16:00 close to 09:30 open, per-leg slippage, minute-level entry and exit drift, NVDL vs NVDX liquidity, spreads and print quality, and net per-night EV after costs
key_findings: Overall: execution costs do not overturn v1.5. After realistic costs the NVDA-2x core beats the old METU x2 + NVDL x1 basket in every cost scenario. The research case is still overstated in two ways: the gross +$0.40/night figure, and NVDX looking worse than NVDL in the model, which comes from bad price data rather than a real difference. Choosing NVDX over NVDL, or the reverse, is worth at most about $0.04 a night either way.

(1) Live vs model, all 53 OVN legs in trades.csv: live +0.138%/leg vs model +0.233%. Slippage mean -0.100% (se 0.185), median -0.371%, sd 1.35%. In dollars, live +$3.28 vs model +$6.57 over about 24 nights. Per-leg slippage is dominated by noise.

Slippage by symbol (mean / median): NVDL n=19 -0.161% / -0.534%; NVDX n=5 +0.877% / +1.164%; METU n=21 -0.078% / -0.425%; AAPU n=5 -0.636% / -0.849%; AMZU n=3 -0.592% / -0.574%. Pooled NVDA-2x n=24: +0.055% / -0.059%, i.e. no measurable leakage. Non-NVDA legs n=29: -0.228% / -0.513%. The NVDX number is inflated because NVDX's official opening prints sat below the 09:31 price on those nights.

Fill quality is at the touch, and the limit buffer is never used. Entry fill vs the 15:52 1-min open: NVDL -0.7bp, NVDX +1.7bp. Exit fill vs the 09:31 bar typical price: NVDL -2.0bp, NVDX -0.2bp (n=5). Entries filled on average about 18bp inside the ask+0.15% limit. The ask+max(0.02,0.15%) and bid-max(0.02,0.15%) limits are protection caps, not costs. They are the same 0.15% for both funds because 0.15% exceeds 2 cents for both.

(2) Timing drift, 1-min bars. Real 1-min data only exists from 2026-09-01: 30 sessions; earlier minute bars are gap-fill. Entry drift (official close / 15:51 close - 1): NVDL -0.063% (median -0.105%), NVDX -0.074%. First trade to 09:31: NVDL -0.090%, NVDX -0.100%, both t about -0.9. Live-equivalent (15:51 to 09:31) minus model over 29 nights: NVDL -0.233% (sd 0.91, t about -1.4).

Timing drift, longer sample: 5-min bars, 162 sessions from 2026-02-23 to 10-13. Close / ~15:52 proxy - 1: NVDL -0.025% (se 0.050), NVDX -0.056% (se 0.052). First trade to 09:35: NVDL +0.065%, NVDX +0.082%. On these nights the tradable 15:52 to next-09:35 return was +0.335% (NVDL) and +0.327% (NVDX) vs the model's +0.325% / +0.290%. Conclusion: no long-run evidence that the 8-minute early entry or the 09:31:05 exit costs much. The 30-night shortfall is mostly first-minute noise.

Late-day momentum is not usable. Conditioning on information known at 15:50 (sign vs today's open or vs the prior close), entry drift is about -0.02% to -0.07% in all four buckets, none with |t| above 0.8. The apparent up-day/down-day effect only appears when you condition on the close itself, which is look-ahead.

NVDX is measurably less liquid than NVDL. Market cap $0.44B vs $4.02B. Average volume 3.2-3.8M vs 9.4-9.6M shares. Median dollar volume in the 15:52 bar $123k vs $295k, and in the 09:31 bar $334k vs $2.38M. Midday minutes with no trades: 10.0% vs 0.2%. Roll spread estimate 15:45-15:59: 5.0bp vs 1.4bp. A 1-cent tick is 4.9bp of NVDX vs 2.7bp of NVDL, so the research note's 'one cent each, so cost unchanged' is wrong in percentage terms.

NVDX's auction prints are worse, and NVDX costs slightly more to hold at our times. Its closing print vs last trade averages -1.7bp (t -2.0, sd 10.7bp) vs NVDL +1.1bp (sd 8.1bp). Its official open vs first trade has sd 0.37% vs 0.09%. Paired with NVDL, NVDX loses 2.8bp more from 15:52 to the close (t -3.1). Over the full hold, NVDX minus NVDL tradable return is: -2.4bp (se 0.9) to the next first trade; -0.8bp (se 0.8) to 09:35; -0.6bp (sd 6.1bp, n=29) on 1-min data. For 5 shares, none of this is material: the extra cost is about 3-6bp per dollar per night.

The m_NVDL = 0.46% vs m_NVDX = 0.42% split built into v1.5's sizing is a data artifact. Most of the 3.9bp gap comes from two NVDX nights. (a) 2025-12-24 was an ex-dividend date ($0.57 distribution). Daily bars are split-adjusted only, so the night shows -4.3% where NVDL showed -1.4%. (b) On 2026-09-08 the official open printed 20.85 while the first trade was 21.79, a fake -4.3% vs NVDL. Corrected over 259 nights: NVDL +0.445%, NVDX +0.435%, difference -1.0bp (se 1.0). Using first-trade opens over 162 nights the difference is +0.3bp (se 1.2).

(3) Net expected edge at E=105.38, using 10/13 closes. Central case (full-year base, 1c spreads): NVDX x5 $0.366/night, NVDL1+NVDX3 $0.363, NVDL2+NVDX1 $0.361, old METU2+NVDL1 $0.119. Recent case (162-night base 0.334%, 2c spread at the open): $0.227 / $0.234 / $0.241 / $0.063. Pessimistic case: $0.101 / $0.120 / $0.140 / -$0.046.

When NVDX x5 is better: it beats NVDL2+NVDX1 only if NVDX's per-dollar disadvantage is below about 0.11 x the net edge. That threshold is 4.3bp in the central case, 2.9bp recent and 1.8bp pessimistic, against an estimated disadvantage of 3.7-6.6bp. So the two are effectively tied, and NVDL-heavy is slightly favored unless the edge is at the high end.

Night 25 (NVDX x5): limit 20.51, filled 20.4699, which is 19.6bp inside the limit and the ask at that time. The 10/13 close was 20.55, so the 15:52 entry gained +0.39% vs the model's close entry. Pre-market quote at about 08:06 ET on 10/14: NVDL 36.19/36.28 and NVDX 20.35/20.40, both about 25bp wide pre-market, so this does not show spreads at 09:31.

The 0.46/0.42 split comes from NVDX's unadjusted $0.57 ex-dividend night (2025-12-24) and a bad official open on 2026-09-08. When two baskets are within about $0.02/night EV, break the tie toward more NVDL. NVDX x5 is acceptable, but it only wins when the net edge is above about 0.4%/night; at the recent-era edge, NVDL2+NVDX1 is $0.01-0.04/night better.

Restate the v1.5 expected effect as a net figure: about $0.37/night (full-year base), about $0.23 (162-night base) and about $0.10 (pessimistic), instead of $0.40 gross. Keep the 15:52 entry. The long-sample drift is -2.5bp (NVDL) and -5.6bp (NVDX), not significant, with no conditional pattern using information known at 15:50. Moving to about 15:55 would recover a few bp at most and squeeze the 15:58 cancel deadline. Not worth a rule change unless the in-turn loop is proven reliable.

Keep the 09:31:05 exit. There is no long-run evidence of a systematic first-minute cost (first trade to 09:35 is +6.5bp / +8.2bp over 162 sessions). Optional 10-night experiment: queue the exit as a regular-hours limit at about bid-1% at 09:29 so it executes at the open. This would bring live returns in line with the model and remove first-minute variance (sd 0.59% NVDL, 1.10% NVDX).

Add ex-dividend handling. NVDX pays an annual distribution (last $0.57, ex 2025-12-24), so on the late-December ex-date the open drop is the dividend, not a loss. Do not let it trigger PAUSE, the edge-decay check or rank changes. Before the 10/27 entry, verify NVDL's listed ex-dividend date of 2026-10-28; the fundamentals fields are inconsistent (payable/record dates in 2023).

Correct BASKET-20261013.md §4: '1 cent each, so execution cost unchanged' is wrong in percentage terms. One cent is 4.9bp of NVDX vs 2.7bp of NVDL, and the 09:50 snapshot is not representative of the 09:31 exit.
caveats: Real 1-minute bars only exist from 2026-09-01 (30 sessions); earlier 1-min data is interpolated gap-fill. Real 5-minute bars only exist from 2026-02-23 (162 sessions). So first-minute exit drift is estimated from 30 sessions only, and the 15:52 price is proxied by the 15:50 5-min bar midpoint. Vs 1-min data that proxy errs by sd 0.17-0.19% per day, with mean bias +1.6 to +2.9bp.

No historical quote (bid/ask) data was available. Spreads come from journal quotes (1 cent at 15:40 and 09:50), fills vs minute prices, and Roll estimates. The actual NVDX spread at 09:31 is unmeasured; the pre-market snapshot (about 25bp for both) is not representative.

Live NVDX sample is n=5 legs, and per-leg slippage sd is 1.0-1.7%. No per-symbol mean slippage is statistically significant; only the paired NVDX-NVDL entry drift (t -3.1) and the closing-print bias (t -2.0) are.

The scenario edge inputs (base, drift, spreads) are my assumptions built from the measured components. The ranking between NVDX x5 and NVDL-heavy flips within the uncertainty, and every difference is at most $0.04/night against a nightly sd of about $2.9.
Night 25's exit happens at 09:31 on 10/14, after this analysis (run around 08:00 ET), so it is not included.

This lens does not address whether the NVDA-2x overnight edge persists (the 162-night base of 0.33% is below the full-year 0.445%), concentration or tail risk, or the earnings blackout. Those belong to other lenses.

reports.lens: TAIL RISK & SIZING (97% of equity in 2x NVDA overnight under v1.5)
key_findings: CORE IDEA SURVIVES, SIZE DOES NOT. Kelly does not condemn NVDA-2x overnight. f* = mu/var is 4.97 on the 1-year data, 1.72 on 7.8 years of synthetic 2x NVDA (2019-01 to 2026-10) and 1.45 on 2019 to 2025-09 only. So 97% is below full Kelly in every model except the pessimistic ones (mean minus 2 standard errors gives f* = 0.24; 2022 alone gives f* < 0). It also maximises median equity and P(reaching $200) in every model. What breaks is the stated -20%-from-high PAUSE constraint, which is a volatility constraint, not a growth one.

THE EVIDENCE WINDOW IS NVDA'S CALMEST REGIME. NVDL overnight = 1.985 x NVDA overnight (corr 0.998, residual sd 0.17%), so NVDA's own history is a valid proxy. At 97% invested with NVDA-earnings nights in cash, nightly sd is 2.54% in the 1-year window versus 3.50% over 2019 to 2025-09. The worst night is -8.1% versus -28.6%. The 2026 year-to-date maxDD is -17.0%, against -78.0% in 2022, -63.9% in 2020 and -55.4% in 2025. Current rolling-60 sd (2.39%) sits at the 23rd percentile of 2019-2026.

SINGLE-NIGHT GAP RISK THAT THE EARNINGS BLACKOUT DOES NOT COVER. In 7.8 years there were 4 non-earnings nights where 97% in 2x NVDA loses 20% or more of equity in one night: 2019-01-28 -28.6% (guidance pre-announcement), 2024-08-05 -27.5%, 2025-01-27 -24.2% (DeepSeek), 2020-03-16 -22.9%. There were 9 nights of -15% or worse and 16 of -10% or worse. At the historical rate of 0.21%/night, P(at least one instant-PAUSE night) is 11.7% in 60 nights, 22.9% in 125 and 40.6% in 250. DeepSeek arrived from a median-volatility regime (prior-60 sd at the 55th percentile), so today's calm offers only partial protection.

IN-SAMPLE NEAR MISS. Even in the calm year, the v1.5 curve (NVDX at 97%, earnings nights in cash) had maxDD -19.3% (2025-11-10 to 2025-11-25), 0.7 points short of PAUSE. The worst 5-night path was -12.9% and the worst 20-night path -17.7%. Six 5-night windows were at -10% or worse. The longest underwater stretch was 60 nights.

BOOTSTRAP, 1-YEAR NVDX EX-EARNINGS (block 5, 2000 paths, 60 nights, start $105, PAUSE = 0.80 x running high). At f = 0.50 / 0.70 / 0.85 / 0.97: P(PAUSE) 0.3 / 3.4 / 9.4 / 15.1%; P(KILL) 0% at every fraction; median terminal equity $116.5 / $121.2 / $124.6 / $127.3; 5th percentile $98.1 / $95.3 / $93.0 / $91.2. The 97% PAUSE figure ranges 12.5-15.1% across seeds.

BOOTSTRAP, 7.8-YEAR SYNTHETIC 2x NVDA (ex-earnings, -0.05%/night tracking drag), same 60-night setup. At f = 0.50 / 0.70 / 0.85 / 0.97: P(PAUSE) 9.0 / 26.6 / 37.1 / 44.8%; P(KILL) 0.0 / 0.0 / 0.2 / 0.5%; median $112.8 / $115.5 / $117.5 / $118.7; 5th percentile $89.0 / $83.0 / $78.4 / $74.8. Using only 2019 to 2025-09 data at 97%: P(PAUSE) 50.5%, P(KILL) 0.9%, 5th percentile $68.5.

FULL GOAL HORIZON (250 nights, 97%). On the 1-year data: P(PAUSE) about 57%, P(KILL) 0%, median $226, P(>= $200) 61-63%. On the 7.8-year data: P(PAUSE) 94%, P(KILL) 6.7%, 5th percentile $49.5, P(>= $200) 35%. On 2019 to 2025-09: P(KILL) 10.2%. Modelling the actual §6 response (rolling-20 high, then 1 NVDL share for 5 nights) changes 97% to P(PAUSE) 35% / P(KILL) 0% on the 1-year data and 91% / 4.3% on the 7.8-year data. A 6-month $200 target needs about 0.52%/night log growth, but the in-sample overnight log growth at 97% is only 0.307%, so P(>= $200 in 125 nights) is 16-18% even in the optimistic model.

THE BASKET DOC'S COMPARISON IS BIASED IN v1.5's FAVOUR. The old basket's 'same sd' (+0.18%/2.76) includes METU's four META-earnings nights (-22.1, +21.0, -15.4, -20.7%), which the old rules had already blacked out. Meanwhile NVDL's score of 0.17 counts NVDA-earnings nights (+9.7, +12.3%) that v1.5 now holds in cash. Like for like, with blackouts: v1.5 NVDX scores +0.346%/2.64% = 0.131, NVDL +0.384%/2.62% = 0.147, and the old 2/3 METU + 1/3 NVDL +0.253%/2.17% = 0.116. The Sharpe gain is marginal, not 0.17 vs 0.07, and v1.5's nightly variance is 1.48x the old basket's.

v1.5 VERSUS OLD BASKET IN THE BOOTSTRAP. On the 1-year data at 60 nights: P(PAUSE) 13.9% (v1.5 at 97%) vs 5.1% (old METU2+NVDL1 at 93%); median $126 vs $120. On the 7.8-year data: 44.6% vs 29.4%. P(KILL in 250 nights) is 6.9% vs 3.8%. v1.5 buys roughly +6-8% median equity at 60 nights for roughly 1.5-2.7x the PAUSE probability.

THE SIZING RULE HAS NO RISK TERM. §3(c) maximises a*lim*m + b*lim*m subject to cost <= 0.98E. With m > 0 that always buys as much notional as fits, so risk is handled only by the PAUSE/KILL triggers, which act after the loss. §6's own reasoning ('a 2-name basket at ~85% caps a repeat near -10% of E') no longer holds under v1.5 and was not updated. A DeepSeek-size NVDA gap now costs about 24% of E in one night. The PAUSE fallback (1 NVDL share) is still 100% NVDA.

NVDX IS THE WEAKER NVDA-2x WRAPPER. Its overnight alpha against 2x NVDA is -0.067%/night versus -0.029% for NVDL, and its residual sd is 0.38% versus 0.17%. Its ex-earnings mean is 0.346% versus 0.384% for NVDL. §3(c) feeds in m_NVDX = 0.42%, which includes the earnings nights v1.5 sits out. Night 25's NVDX x5 is the lower-quality way to reach 97%.

SECOND NAME (part 4): no low-correlation candidate has a robust positive overnight mean, so diversification is no better than holding cash. In the 1-year data with own-earnings blackouts: AAPU +0.027% (corr 0.11), GGLL +0.073% (0.33), AMZU +0.037% (0.45), METU +0.187% (0.29, but -0.111% in the first half of the year). Over the long run, 2x META and 2x GOOGL are each about +0.014%/night. Names with real means are highly correlated or unaffordable: TSMX 0.71/$88, FNGU 0.70/$37, TQQQ 0.78/$81, SPXL 0.75/$298; long-run 3x IWM +0.15% has corr 0.65 but TNA costs $58. On the 1-year data, 70% NVDX + 27% METU gives P(PAUSE 60n) 6.0% and median $149 at 125 nights, versus 12.5% / $155 for 97% NVDX and 2.5% / $141 for 70% NVDX alone. On the long-run data, 70/27 combinations give P(PAUSE 60n) 35-38% versus 44.8% for 97% NVDA and 26.9% for 70% NVDA plus cash. Cutting the NVDA fraction does most of the work; the satellite adds little.

SIZE CHOICES THAT RESPECT THE PAUSE LIMIT (whole shares at E = 105, NVDX about $20.47, NVDL about $36.36). Reachable fractions: 54% (NVDL1+NVDX1), 58% (NVDX3), 69% (NVDL2), 73.5% (NVDL1+NVDX2), 78% (NVDX4), 88.6% (NVDL2+NVDX1), 93% (NVDL1+NVDX3), 97% (NVDX5). P(PAUSE) at 60 / 125 nights, 1-year data: 69% gives 3 / 9%, 78% gives 6 / 16%, 97% gives 15 / 33%. On the 7.8-year data: 69% gives 27 / 52%, 97% gives 46 / 75%. Log growth on the 1-year data is 0.229%/night at 70% and 0.307% at 97%: 282 versus 210 nights from $105 to $200, overnight leg only.

NVDA earnings nights in sample, NVDL: +9.7% (11/20), -1.7% (2/26), -1.2% (5/21), +12.3% (8/27). META earnings nights, METU: -22.1, +21.0, -15.4, -20.7%

v1.5 NVDX at 97%, NVDA earnings in cash: mean +0.336%, sd 2.56%, mean log +0.302%, worst night -8.3% (2025-11-25), worst 5-night -12.9%, worst 20-night -17.7%, maxDD -19.3% (11/10 to 11/25/2025), longest underwater 60 nights
Old METU2+NVDL1 (59.6% + 33.6% of E) with blackouts: mean +0.241%, sd 2.01%, worst night -4.4%, worst 20-night -20.4%, maxDD -21.4%, longest underwater 129 nights. Without blackouts: maxDD -24.8%

Like-for-like at 100% invested: NVDX ex-earnings 0.346% / 2.64% (score 0.131); NVDL ex-earnings 0.384% / 2.62% (0.147); old basket with blackouts 0.253% / 2.17% (0.116); doc's numbers were 0.17 vs 0.066

Bootstrap, 60 nights, 1y NVDX with mean cut to zero: P(PAUSE) 4.1 / 18.3 / 30.8 / 40.5%. With mean cut by 1 standard error (+0.184%): 1.3 / 8.2 / 17.4 / 25.1%
Rule-realistic run (rolling-20 high, 35% invested for 5 nights after PAUSE, HWM 107.11), 60 nights at 97%: PAUSE 8.5% (1y) / 41.9% (7.8y) / 48.4% (2019 to 2025-09)
v1.5 vs old basket at 60 / 125 / 250 nights, 1y: P(PAUSE) 13.9 / 32.5 / 56.1% vs 5.1 / 15.0 / 31.4%. 7.8y at 60 nights: 44.6% vs 29.4%; 7.8y KILL at 250 nights: 6.9% vs 3.8%

Kelly f* = mu/var: 1y 4.97; 1y mean minus 1 se 2.61; 1y mean minus 2 se 0.24; 7.8y 1.72 (empirical argmax 1.55); 2019 to 2025-09 1.45 (empirical argmax 1.32); 2022 -2.63. So 97% is 0.20 / 0.56 / 0.67 of Kelly under the 1y / 7.8y / 2019 to 2025-09 estimates

70% NVDX + 27% X, 1y data, P(PAUSE 60n) and median at 125n: METU 6.0% / $149; SPXL 6.9% / $148; AAPU 3.8% / $142; FNGU 9.1% / $152; MUU 18.5% / $190. Benchmarks: 97% NVDX 12.5% / $155; 70% NVDX 2.5% / $141

Long-run synthetic overnight means: 2x META +0.014%, 2x GOOGL +0.014%, 3x QQQ +0.100% (corr 0.82), 3x SPY +0.056% (0.75), 3x IWM +0.147% (0.65). Long-run P(PAUSE 60n): 70/27 combinations 35-38% vs 97% NVDA 44.8% vs 70% NVDA 26.9%

Current rolling-60 sd of 2x NVDA overnight: 2.39%, 23rd percentile of 2019-2026 (median 2.74%, 90th percentile 4.95%). Volatility before the big gaps: 2020-03-16 at the 93rd percentile, 2024-08-05 79th, 2025-01-27 55th, 2022-08-08 77th
recommended_changes: Add a risk term to §3(c). Replace pure EV maximisation (which always fills 0.98E) with a cap. Recommended: NVDA-2x notional <= about 75% of E (NVDL x2 = 69% or NVDL1+NVDX2 = 73.5% at E = 105), remainder in cash. On 1y data this cuts P(PAUSE in 60 nights) from about 13-15% to about 3-4% and on 7.8y data from about 45% to about 27-30%. The cost is about 25% of log growth (0.307 to 0.229%/night on 1y data).

Or use volatility targeting: invested fraction = min(0.97, 2.0% / trailing-60 sd of NVDA-2x overnight returns). Today that is about 0.81 (NVDX x4 = 78%), and it falls to about 0.4-0.5 in the high-vol regimes (77-93rd percentile) that preceded 3 of the 4 worst gaps.

Prefer NVDL over NVDX when whole shares allow (NVDL1+NVDX3 = 93% or NVDL2 = 69% instead of NVDX5). NVDX lags 2x NVDA by about 0.04%/night more than NVDL and has twice the tracking noise. Use ex-earnings means in §3(c): NVDX 0.346%, NVDL 0.384%.

Fix §6's reasoning. Under v1.5 a single NVDA gap of -10% to -15% (16 such nights at 2x in 7.8 years, unrelated to earnings) costs 19-29% of E in one night and triggers PAUSE at once. The earnings blackout does not cover guidance pre-announcements, export-control news or macro shocks. Also make the PAUSE fallback less than 100% NVDA, or cash.

Correct BASKET-20261013.md. The old-versus-new comparison must apply the old rule's META-earnings blackout and remove NVDA-earnings nights from v1.5. Like for like, the score is 0.131 (NVDX) vs 0.116 (old), not 0.17 vs 0.07, and v1.5's variance is 1.48x the old basket's. Also restate expected returns: about +0.34%/night at 97% in-sample, not +0.40%, before about 0.07%/leg execution cost, and probably about +0.20%/night on the 7.8-year evidence.
Don't add a satellite to diversify: no low-correlation name in the data has a robust positive overnight mean. Lower the NVDA fraction and hold cash instead.

State the goal tension explicitly. $200 in 6 months needs about 0.52%/night log growth, above even the in-sample 97% rate (0.307%). P(>= $200 in 125 nights) is 16-18% at 97% on the 1y data and about 11% on the 7.8y data. A 12-month target at about 75% invested is the defensible framing.
caveats: The 7.8-year series is synthetic: 2 x NVDA close-to-open minus 0.05%/night drag, NVDA-earnings nights removed. It is checked against NVDL (beta 1.985, corr 0.998) but includes 2019-2022, before NVDL existed. It also ignores the 09:30-to-09:31:05 fill noise (-3.4% to +2.8% per the WEEKEND doc), which adds variance.

Earnings dates before 2025-05 (NVDA) and 2025-04 (META) came from memory, not the tool. They were checked: META's flagged nights have median |gap| 7.9% versus 0.6% on all nights, and none of the 15 worst non-earnings NVDA nights is a known earnings date.

The bootstraps model only the overnight leg. The TZA day leg (85-95% of E on up to 3 days in 5) adds variance, so real PAUSE odds are somewhat higher. The headline runs do not model the PAUSE response; a separate run with the §6 response is reported.

PAUSE is defined two ways. The task uses 0.80 x running high; RULES §6 uses 0.80 x rolling 20-session high, which is looser (60-night 1y P(PAUSE) at 97%: 13.9% running vs 9.1% rolling-20). Both are reported. Monte Carlo noise is about +/-1.5 points at 2000 paths.
Fractions are applied as continuous nightly rebalancing. Whole shares give only the discrete fractions listed, and those drift as prices and E change.

Kelly figures rest on means with t of about 2.1 (1y) and 2.7 (7.8y). NVDL was picked post hoc from a 15-name universe, so the 1y mean likely carries winner's-curse bias, and the 7.8y figure (+0.213%/night ex-earnings) is the better central estimate. Both include NVDA's exceptional 2019-2026 rally.

Peer-earnings nights (GOOGL/META/AMZN/AAPL/MU pm, TSM am) were not more volatile for NVDX in the 1y sample (sd 2.48%, mean +0.99%, n = 19). I found no evidence for extra event blackouts beyond NVDA's own earnings.

reports.lens: IMPROVEMENT SEARCH: alternative and complementary overnight carriers to NVDA-2x (60 leveraged-long products scanned on 1y ETF data, plus 20 underlyings over 10y)
key_findings: CORE SURVIVES. Scan: 60 leveraged-long ETFs, 46 distinct underlyings, 250 nights to 2026-10-13. On model prints NVDL ranks #2 by score (0.153). Only DFEN (3x aerospace & defense) beats it, at 0.169. MVLL (0.149) and MUU/MULL (0.147/0.146) tie within noise (SE of a 250-night score is about 0.063) but carry 2.5x the sd (6.8-7.0%). METU's 250-night score is 0.013, which confirms dropping it.

DFEN IS A MODEL ARTIFACT (an important hole in rule (b)). On model prints DFEN literally passes v1.5 (b): score 0.169 >= 0.153 and ex-4-largest-gap mean +0.299% > 0.25%. So 'none qualifies on 10/13' was only true inside the 14-name universe. DFEN is thin: 0.26M shares/day, below §2's 1M minimum, and 71% of its 1-minute bars have no trade (NVDL: 30%). Its official open print is systematically above what can be sold at 09:31: open to 09:31 averaged -0.50%/night (t -3.1, n=22, 1-minute bars); open to 09:35 averaged -0.26%/night (t -2.3, n=159, 5-minute bars, Feb-Oct 2026). On a 15:55->09:35 basis, NVDL/DFEN 50/50 scores 0.101 versus NVDL alone 0.111, while on model prints the same pair scores 0.154 versus 0.119. The underlying edge is real: ITA has the best 10-year overnight score of 20 underlyings (0.100 vs NVDA 0.095) and ranked #1 in each of the last 3 Oct-Sep years. But no liquid, affordable leveraged-long defense product was found to capture it.

LOW-CORRELATION CANDIDATES FAIL. LLYX has correlation 0.05 to NVDL, but its edge is all earnings (ex-earnings mean +0.084%). AAPU/AAPB (correlation about 0) have no edge (score about 0). Broad-index leveraged ETFs (SSO, UPRO, QLD, TQQQ, SPXL; scores 0.08-0.10) are too correlated (0.74-0.77) to pass even the marginal-Sharpe test. TSM-2x is robust over 10 years (score 0.095, 9/10 years positive), but TSMX costs $85 (cannot fit next to the core at E=$105) and TSMU is illiquid (0.04M shares/day).

MU-2x IS A MOMENTUM BET, NOT A DIVERSIFIER. Basket: MULL x1 + NVDL x1 + NVDX x2 ($20 MULL leg, 6M shares/day, no open-print bias). With real earnings blackouts it beats NVDX x5 in both halves of the year: E$/night +0.376 vs +0.277 and +0.478 vs +0.359; score 0.130 vs 0.097 and 0.153 vs 0.142. But maxDD is worse (-24% vs -20%). Over 10 years MU's overnight score is 0.077 (NVDA 0.095), MU was negative in 3 of 10 years, and this year's 62.9bp/night is about 4x its 10-year average of 16.4bp. A 10-year NVDA 0.8 / MU 0.2 blend did not improve growth (x438 vs x709 ex-top-4 gaps) and left the 10-year maxDD unchanged (-82%). MVLL is the same story.

RULE (b) USES THE WRONG TEST AND IS INCONSISTENT. Adding a satellite raises basket Sharpe whenever score_X > rho * score_core, not when score_X >= score_core. Under the correct test, 11 non-NVDA names pass on 10/13. Rule (b) also compares the satellite's all-nights score against a core score inflated by NVDA earnings nights that v1.5 skips (+9.7% and +12.3% gaps): NVDL all-nights 0.153 vs ex-earnings 0.135. On ex-earnings scores, MVLL (0.141) beats NVDL (0.135) and would qualify. Qualification is therefore a coin flip decided by definitions.

WALK-FORWARDS DO NOT SHOW A ROBUST BETTER BASKET. 1-year ETF data, 120-night lookback, rebalanced every 21 nights: NVDL alone 0.142, v1.5 satellite rule 0.144, marginal-Sharpe satellite 0.146, top-2 ranking 0.127 (maxDD -42%). With a 60-night lookback, both satellite rules came out below NVDL alone. 10-year synthetic test (5bp/night drag, top-4-gap-per-year earnings proxy, 250-night lookback): NVDA-2x alone has the best log growth (+0.242%/night, score 0.093); marginal-Sharpe satellite 0.094 / +0.215; NVDA 2/3 + ITA-3x 1/3 0.093 / +0.211; top-2 ranking 0.077. Raw (no blackout), top-2 ranking looked best (0.104, maxDD -51%), but that advantage came from earnings gaps.

NVDA-2x HAS A CONCENTRATION TAIL THAT NO CARRIER FIXES. In the 10-year synthetic test NVDA-2x overnight-only had maxDD -86% raw and -82% with the earnings proxy (peak 2022-02-02, trough Feb-Mar 2023). Blending in ITA-3x only cuts this to -68 to -73%, because every overnight carrier loses in bear-market years (Oct21-Sep22 year: NVDA -13.6bp/night unlevered). This is a regime problem, not a basket problem.

SIZING (c) AND THE EXPECTED-VALUE CLAIM. NVDL tracks NVDA-2x better than its siblings: NVDL minus NVDX +4.1bp/night (t 1.77), NVDL minus NVDU +4.6bp/night (t 2.23). With real blackouts, the held NVDX x5 earned +0.303%/night (sd 2.58, score 0.118, maxDD -20%). NVDL x2 + NVDX x1 earned the same dollars (+$0.319 vs +$0.318 per night at E=105) with sd 2.33, score 0.131 and maxDD -17%, and beat NVDX x5 in both halves. The memo's '+$0.40/night' is overstated: ex-earnings at 98% invested it is about +$0.32 gross, roughly +$0.25 after the ~0.07%/leg live cost found in the 10/10 weekend research.

MULTIPLE TESTING. Across 46 distinct underlyings the best 1-year t-stat is 2.68; NVDL's is 2.42 all nights and about 2.1 ex-earnings. One year of data alone cannot separate NVDA from selection luck. The support comes from the 10-year data: NVDA overnight was positive in 9 of 10 years with a top-3 10-year score. Cross-sectional persistence is moderate: Spearman correlation of first-half vs second-half means across the 46 underlyings is 0.52, and year-over-year score rank correlation ranged from -0.20 to +0.67.

judge.rationale:
All six reviewers agree on the direction: no one argues to revert, and every 'weakens' verdict attacks the size of the claimed edge and the specific clauses, not the switch itself. I re-checked the disputed points against the data files; scripts are in /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-test-trading/0c00e7d9-c916-50ae-ac83-8f6429819f25/scratchpad/wf/judge/.

(1) The BASKET-20261013 headline comparison is wrong. With each basket in cash on its own earnings nights, as both rulebooks require, over 257 nights NVDL makes +0.384%/night (sd 2.62, score 0.147) and old METU2+NVDL1 makes +0.253% (sd 2.17, score 0.116). The difference is +0.131%/night with t=1.01. Over the last 137 nights the old basket is ahead (-0.053%, t=-0.26). Over the last 60 they are tied (+0.098%, t=0.34). 'Worst in every window' and '+$0.40 vs +$0.18' do not hold.

(2) Picking NVDA is hindsight. No ex-ante long-window rule picks it, and NVDL's lead over an equal-weight universe is t of about 1.1. However, the rule v1.5 replaced, the 30-night rank, has no predictive power (monthly IC about 0). A realistic whole-share version of old §3 scores about 0.08 at about 70% invested, against about 0.14-0.15 for fixed NVDA-2x out of sample. NVDA-2x is also positive over the long run: synthetic 2x NVDA ex-earnings over 7.8 years averages +0.22%/night, though 2022 was -45bp/night. So a fixed NVDA-2x core is a reasonable, simple, low-churn choice. It is not a proven better one, and the planning edge should be about +0.30%/night gross per unit of exposure, not +0.46%.

(3) Rule (b) is broken. On the agent's own 10/9 file, MUU's 250-night score was 0.1598 against NVDL's 0.1572, so MUU qualified. The comparison sits inside one standard error (about 0.063), and walk-forward tests show satellites add nothing.

(4) The m_NVDL vs m_NVDX split in (c) is a data artifact. Adding back NVDX's 2025-12-24 distribution and fixing the 2026-09-08 bad open gives NVDX +0.448% vs NVDL +0.458%, a difference of 1.0bp (t=0.97). NVDX also costs about 3-6bp more per night to trade.

(5) Sizing. 97% is below full Kelly even on the 7.8-year data (f* 1.80; 1.15 with the mean cut by one standard error), so heavy exposure is defensible for a growth goal. NVDX x5 is still effectively dominated: NVDL2+NVDX1 has about the same EV per night after costs with about 9% less exposure. Filling NVDL first naturally lands at about 79-98% invested, about 89% tonight.

(6) The largest risk is a bear regime, not a single night: 7.8-year maxDD is -81% at 97%. A trailing-120-night edge-decay switch, checked on Mondays, cut that to -61% and cut 2022 from -73% to -24% with no loss of growth. It would never have fired in the past 257 nights. That makes it the cheapest robust protection, and it matches the statistics lens's pre-registered review trigger.

At NVDL ~36.10 and NVDX ~20.30 with the +0.15% limit buffer, the limit cost is about 72.31 + 20.33 = 92.64, about 88.6% of E=104.6. The cap is 0.98E = 102.51, leaving about $12 cash. Compute it live at 15:52 by filling NVDL first: buy NVDL up to the cap, then add NVDX shares while the total stays <= 0.98E. If NVDL is <= ~34.15 at 15:52, that gives NVDL x3 (~98%). If an NVDL fill moves, recompute the NVDX count from the remaining cap. Do not hold NVDX x5: that adds ~9% exposure for about the same EV per night after costs. No non-NVDA name. No earnings blackout applies (next NVDA report is 11/17 pm).
judge.sizing_recommendation: Fill NVDL first under the existing 0.98*E cap, then NVDX as filler. Use no m inputs and no optimizer. That puts the invested fraction at roughly 79-98% depending on prices (88.6% tonight). The case for keeping exposure high: full Kelly on the 7.8-year synthetic 2x NVDA is 1.80 (1.15 with the mean cut by one standard error). Log growth per night is 0.340% at 97% vs 0.313% at 88.6% (1y data) and 0.153% vs 0.145% (7.8y). So cutting to a fixed 69-75% gives up 20-27% of growth for a goal that needs growth. The bigger risk is a regime, not a single night, so the §3(f) trailing-120 edge-decay switch (to cash) does more than a lower fixed cap: maxDD -61% vs -71% for a fixed 75% on the 7.8y data, with higher growth. Keep PAUSE sizing at 1 NVDL share (~35% of E). I am not adopting a volatility brake (trailing-60 ex-earnings sd > 3.5% -> 1 NVDL share). It helped on the 7.8y data (log growth 0.178% vs 0.153%, maxDD -59% vs -81%), but the benefit vanished at a 4.5% threshold, so it is threshold-sensitive. gaps: The biggest gap is that nobody modelled the TZA day leg and the overnight leg together. The day leg is active: 12 active days, running 3 days in every 5 at about 90% of E. Every PAUSE and KILL figure behind the judge's sizing decision covers the overnight leg only. I bootstrapped both legs together (60-night horizon, block 5, E0 104.6, rolling-20 high, TP +1% simulated from the daily high, 3-on/2-off schedule). P(PAUSE) at 88.6% overnight goes from 4.9% to 20.5% on 1-year data and from 35.9% to 47.0% on the 7.8-year synthetic. At 97% it goes from 7.4% to 24.5% and from 41.1% to 52.3%. Over 125 nights at 88.6% on 1-year data it goes from 9.0% to 39.9%. A Gaussian iid check agrees: 5.1% to 14.8%. Over a full year the day leg shows no edge. With the TP rule applied to TZA daily bars it averages -0.026%/day (sd 1.92%, skew -1.89, TP hit on 71% of days, 5th percentile -4.5%). The 7.8-year synthetic -3x IWM version averages +0.017%/day. So the day leg adds most of the short-horizon PAUSE risk while showing no long-sample edge. The judge's argument that cutting overnight exposure costs growth for little PAUSE reduction ignores it; if risk has to come down, the day leg is the cheaper cut. Caveat: live day legs net about +$3.25 over 12 legs (state.json), and open/close are proxies for the 09:32 entry and 15:49 exit.

§3(f) edge-decay switch: the judge's 'no loss of growth / no in-sample cost' claim is overstated. I reproduced the judge's numbers exactly (W120 Monday: log growth 0.155% vs 0.153%, maxDD -60.8% vs -81.0%, 2022 -24% vs -73%). But all of the growth parity comes from 2022. Excluding 2022, the switch cuts mean log growth from 0.253% to 0.194%/night, about 23% lower. It cost money in the V-shaped recoveries: 2025 +9% becomes -33% (OFF 2025-04-07 to 07-28), 2020 +100% becomes +39% (OFF 2020-03-09 to 06-29), 2019 +45% becomes +17%. Growth moves from 0.153 to 0.174 depending on which weekday the re-rank falls, and from 0.134 to 0.203 across W80-200 and thresholds of ±0.1%. The maxDD cut is robust (-35% to -66% vs -81% in every variant). The switch sits close to firing: on the synthetic series it went OFF 2025-09-08 to 09-22, just before the evidence window. The NVDL ETF trailing-120 minimum is +0.052% (window ending 2026-04-28), and 9% of windows sit below +0.10%. It should be presented as insurance that pays in slow bears and costs in fast rebounds, not as free.

The judge's justification for keeping NVDA compares the wrong things. It sets a hindsight-picked fixed NVDA-2x (score 0.14-0.15) against an ex-ante old rule (0.075-0.085). An ex-ante version of v1.5's own procedure scored 0.064-0.074, so procedure against procedure the switch is no better. Only one lens (selection-bias) computed the 'realistic old §3' number. It approximated sizing (no v1.2 partial unit, fixed E, 68% invested even though v1.1 targets at least 70%) and nobody cross-checked it. Invested fraction does not change the mean/sd score, so the 'at about 70% invested' framing does not explain the gap. The defensible case is lower variance and less churn, not a demonstrated edge.

The judge's proposed §6 text has a factual error. '-10..-15% NVDA non-earnings gap (16 such nights in 7.8 years)' is wrong. The 16 nights are NVDA gaps of -5.2% or worse, which cost at least 10% of E at 97% x2. NVDA non-earnings gaps of -10% or worse: 4 (2019-01-28 -14.8%, 2024-08-05 -14.2%, 2025-01-27 -12.5%, 2020-03-16 -11.8%). Gaps of -15% or worse: 0. At 88.6% exposure, an instant PAUSE from at-high needs an NVDA gap of about -11.3%; 4 such nights in 7.8 years.

The 2022-11-08 midterm night was -6.0% for 2x NVDA (2020: +5.7%, 2024: +4.4%). §3's 'edge survives macro nights' rests on older research nobody re-checked.
Untested: the alternative PAUSE fallback. 1 NVDL share is still 100% NVDA. The risk lens flagged this and the judge kept it without testing cash or a lower fraction.

critic.summary:
Completeness check of the six lens reports and the judge's modify_v15 decision. None of the gaps changes the top-level decision. No lens shows the old rule is better ex-ante: v1.5's own procedure scores 0.064-0.074 against 0.075-0.085 for the old rule, so procedure against procedure they tie. NVDA-2x has lower variance and churn, and the corrected comparison is a wash rather than a loss. Three findings should change the judge's write-up and sizing rationale.

(1) The day leg was never modelled. The TZA day leg runs at about 90% of E on 3 days in 5, and no lens or the judge modelled it alongside the overnight leg. Bootstrapping both legs together, P(PAUSE in 60 nights) at tonight's 88.6% goes from 4.9% to 20.5% on 1-year data and from 35.9% to 47.0% on the 7.8-year synthetic. Over 125 nights on 1-year data it goes from 9% to 40%. Over a full year the day leg (TP rule simulated on TZA daily bars) shows about zero mean (-0.026%/day, skew -1.89). The judge argued against trimming the overnight core because growth is needed. If the human wants less drawdown, the day leg is the cheaper cut, and the PAUSE odds the judge quoted are understated by roughly 3x on 1-year data.

(2) The §3(f) edge-decay switch is not free. The judge's numbers reproduce exactly. The drawdown cut holds up across every weekday phase, window and threshold I tried (-35% to -66% vs -81%). Growth parity, however, comes entirely from 2022: excluding 2022, the switch cuts log growth about 23% (0.253% to 0.194%/night). It turned 2025 from +9% into -33% and 2020 from +100% into +39%. It nearly fires on the evidence window: NVDL ETF trailing-120 minimum is +0.052%, and the synthetic series fired in September 2025. It should be adopted, if at all, as stated insurance with a known cost.

(3) The judge's §6 text is factually wrong. There were 4 NVDA non-earnings gaps of -10% or worse in 7.8 years, not 16, and none of -15% or worse; the 16 is the count of gaps of -5.2% or worse.

Smaller points:
- The judge's main pro-switch argument compares a hindsight fixed pick against an ex-ante rule. That rests on one lens's approximate 'realistic old §3' sim, which nobody cross-checked.
- 'NVDX x5 dominated' is really a tie.
- Untested: macro event nights inside the hold (CPI/NFP at 08:30; the 2026-11-03 midterm; the 2022 midterm night was -6% at 2x), the 100%-NVDA PAUSE fallback, half-day edge, ETF/issuer risk, and the anomaly's mechanism.
- Confirmed: the judge's overnight-only PAUSE bootstrap numbers (within Monte Carlo noise) and the NVDA 2026-11-17 pm earnings date (Robinhood, verified=true).
